'''Ian Fleming''' (born 4 August 1935) is an [[England|English]] organic chemist, an [[emeritus]] professor of the [[University of Cambridge]], and an emeritus fellow of [[Pembroke College, Cambridge]]. He was the first to determine the full structure of [[chlorophyll]] (in 1967) and was involved in the development of the [[organic synthesis|synthesis]] of [[cyanocobalamin]] by [[Robert Burns Woodward]]. He has made major contributions to the use of [[organosilicon]] compounds for [[Stereoselectivity|stereoselective]] syntheses; reactions which have found application in the synthesis of natural compounds. He is also a prolific author, and has written a number of textbooks, encyclopedia chapters and influential review articles.

==Early life and education==
Ian Fleming was born on 4 August 1935, in [[Kingswinford]], [[Staffordshire]] and grew up in [[Stourbridge]], [[Worcestershire]], where he attended the [[King Edward VI College, Stourbridge|King Edward VI Grammar School for Boys]]. He was accepted to study [[Natural Science Tripos|Natural Sciences]] at [[Pembroke College, Cambridge]] but first joined the [[Royal Corps of Signals]] to complete compulsory [[Conscription in the United Kingdom|National Service]], in 1954–1956. He was commissioned as a [[Second lieutenant#United Kingdom and other Commonwealth countries|second lieutenant]].<ref name=Education>{{cite web |url=http://www-fleming.ch.cam.ac.uk/Studies.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230603123317/http://www-fleming.ch.cam.ac.uk/Studies.html |archive-date=2023-06-03 |title=School and University Studies |last=Fleming |first=Ian |access-date=2025-10-01}}</ref>

He graduated with a [[Bachelor of Arts|B.A.]] in 1959 from the [[University of Cambridge]] and immediately started research in the [[Yusuf Hamied Department of Chemistry|Department of Chemistry]], under the supervision of John Harley-Mason, studying [[decarboxylation|decarboxylative]] elimination and the chemistry of [[enamine]]s. He completed his [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] in 1962.<ref name=Education/><ref name=Simke>{{Cite web |url=https://baranlab.org//images/grpmtgpdf/Simke_Aug_15.pdf |title=Chemists with Named Oxidations |website=baranlab.org |last=Simke |first=Leah |date=2015-08-29 |access-date=2025-09-29}}</ref>

==Career==
Fleming obtained a research fellowship at Pembroke College in 1962. In 1963–1964 he spent a post-doctoral year at [[Harvard University]] with R.B. Woodward working on the [[Vitamin B12 total synthesis|synthesis of vitamin B<sub>12</sub>]]. He returned to Cambridge in autumn 1964 when appointed by [[Lord Todd]] as a University Demonstrator.<ref name=Education/> He was promoted and by 1986 was a [[Reader (academic rank)|Reader]]; in 1998 he became a [[Professor|Professor of Organic Chemistry]]. Throughout the period 1964–2002 he was a Fellow and assistant director of Studies in Natural Sciences at Pembroke College. He was obliged by the statutes of the university to retire in 2002 when he reached the age of 67.<ref name=Simke/><ref name=cv>{{cite web |url=http://www-fleming.ch.cam.ac.uk/CV.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230603111224/http://www-fleming.ch.cam.ac.uk/CV.html |archive-date=2023-06-03 |title=Academic posts |last=Fleming |first=Ian |access-date=2025-10-01}}</ref>

===Teaching===
He has authored popular undergraduate textbooks on [[spectroscopy|spectroscopic]] methods of structure determination, organic synthesis, and applications of [[frontier molecular orbital theory]] to problems in organic chemistry.<ref name=pubs>See selected publications</ref> The book ''Spectroscopic Methods in Organic Chemistry'', which he co-wrote with [[Dudley Williams (biochemist)|Dudley Williams]], was first published in 1966 and had reached edition six and been translated into multiple languages by the time of Williams' death in 2010.<ref name=roysoc>{{cite journal|last1=Sanders|first1=Jeremy&nbsp;K.&nbsp;M.|last2=Robinson|first2=Dame Carol&nbsp;V.|date=31 December 2017|title=Dudley Howard Williams. 25 May 1937 — 3 November 2010|journal=Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society|volume=63|pages=567–583|doi=10.1098/rsbm.2017.0009|doi-access=free}}</ref> Fleming published a seventh edition in 2019, following his teaching a one-semester course on the subject at the [[University of Illinois]] for seven years from 2012 to 2018.<ref name=pubs/> According to [[John Sulston]], Fleming in the 1960s "was young, personable and really sparky about how things worked".<ref>{{cite journal |last=Sulston |first=John |title=Q&A John Sulston |journal=chem@cam |date=Winter 2017 |issue=56 |page=4 |url=https://www.ch.cam.ac.uk/files/chematcam/Chem%40Cam56-website.pdf |access-date=2025-10-01}}</ref>

{{As of|2025}}, although formally retired, Fleming continues to give a course of six lectures on organic spectroscopy to third-year undergraduates in the Cambridge Chemistry Department.<ref>{{cite web |title= B2: Organic spectroscopy |url=https://teaching.ch.cam.ac.uk/files/Start%20of%20Term%20Arrangements/Part%20II%20course%20guide%202025%20.pdf |date=2025 |page=8 |website=teaching.ch.cam.ac.uk |access-date=2025-11-02}}</ref>

===Research===
[[File:Chlorophyll a ring D stereochemistry.svg|thumb|Red and green markers in ring D of chlorophyll ''a'' where absolute stereochemistry was established]]
In 1967, Fleming published a paper which provided the final details of the structure of [[chlorophyll a|chlorophyll ''a'']] by confirming the [[absolute configuration]] of the two sidechains attached to one of the rings of the [[macrocycle]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Fleming |first1=IAN |title=Absolute Configuration and the Structure of Chlorophyll |journal=Nature |date=1967 |volume=216 |issue=5111 |pages=151–152 |doi=10.1038/216151a0 |bibcode=1967Natur.216..151F }}
</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Senge |first1=Mathias |last2=Ryan |first2=Aoife |last3=Letchford |first3=Kristie |last4=MacGowan |first4=Stuart |last5=Mielke |first5=Tamara |title=Chlorophylls, Symmetry, Chirality, and Photosynthesis |journal=Symmetry |date=2014 |volume=6 |issue=3 |page=788 |doi=10.3390/sym6030781 |bibcode=2014Symm....6..781S |doi-access=free |hdl=2262/73843 |hdl-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite book |editor-last=Dolphin |editor-first=David |title=The Porphyrins V2 |publisher=Elsevier |publication-place=New York |date=2012-12-02 |isbn=978-0-323-14956-3 |pages=24–25 |chapter=1 Synthesis and Stereochemistry of Hydroporphyrins |last=Scheer |first=Hugo |url=https://www.google.co.uk/books/edition/The_Porphyrins_V2/lNf9I6HvX1AC?hl=en&gbpv=1&printsec=frontcover&bsq=fleming}}</ref>

In 1971–1972, while on [[sabbatical]] at [[McGill University]], Fleming worked on the synthesis of the highly stable 8-cycloheptatrienylheptafulvenyl [[carbocation]].<ref name=Simke/><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Fleming |first1=Ian |title=Synthesis of the 8-cycloheptatrienylheptafulvenyl cation |journal=Journal of the Chemical Society, Perkin Transactions 1 |date=1973 |page=1019 |doi=10.1039/P19730001019 }}</ref> More significantly, during that period he developed ideas for applying [[silicon]] within organic chemistry.<ref name=Independent>{{cite web |url=http://www-fleming.ch.cam.ac.uk/Independent.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250427153803/http://www-fleming.ch.cam.ac.uk/Independent.html |archive-date=2025-04-27 |title=Independent research |last=Fleming |first=Ian |access-date=2025-10-01}}</ref>
This led to advances in the topic of [[organosilicon]] chemistry for organic synthesis, especially for the [[Stereoselectivity|stereoselective]] production of [[Chirality (chemistry)|chiral]] [[molecule]]s.<ref name=Simke/>
:[[File:Fleming-Tamao oxidation Chem1996.svg]]
His work on what is now called the [[Fleming–Tamao oxidation]] allows the replacement of a carbon-silicon bond with a carbon-oxygen bond in a reaction which is [[stereospecific]] with [[retention of configuration]]. This allows the silicon group to be used as a [[functional group|functional]] equivalent of the [[hydroxyl]] group.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Jones |first1=Graeme R. |last2=Landais |first2=Yannick |title=The oxidation of the carbon-silicon bond |journal=Tetrahedron |date=1996 |volume=52 |issue=22 |pages=7599–7662 |doi=10.1016/S0040-4020(96)00038-5 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Barrett |first1=Anthony G. M. |last2=Head |first2=John |last3=Smith |first3=Marie L. |last4=Stock |first4=Nicholas S. |last5=White |first5=A. J. P. |last6=Williams |first6=D. J. |title=Fleming−Tamao Oxidation and Masked Hydroxyl Functionality: Total Synthesis of (+)-Pramanicin and Structural Elucidation of the Antifungal Natural Product (−)-Pramanicin |journal=The Journal of Organic Chemistry |date=1999 |volume=64 |issue=16 |pages=6005–6018 |doi=10.1021/jo9905672 }}</ref> In the early method shown for the C-Si bond's replacement, two steps are required: treatment with [[fluoroboric acid]] followed by an oxidation using [[meta-Chloroperoxybenzoic acid|''meta''-chloroperoxybenzoic acid]]. A one-step procedure using [[potassium bromide]] and [[peracetic acid]] in [[acetic acid]] has also been described.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Fleming |first1=Ian |last2=Henning |first2=Rolf |last3=Parker |first3=David C. |last4=Plaut |first4=Howard E. |last5=Sanderson |first5=Philip E. J. |title=The phenyldimethylsilyl group as a masked hydroxy group |journal=Journal of the Chemical Society, Perkin Transactions 1 |issue=4 |date=1995 |issn=0300-922X |doi=10.1039/p19950000317 |pages=317–337 }}</ref>

He has over 200 scientific publications, including major contributions to the chemical encyclopedia "Comprehensive Organic Chemistry", and many influential review articles.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.scopus.com/authid/detail.uri?authorId=16156495700 |title=Fleming, Ian |website=scopus.com |publisher=Elsevier |access-date=2025-09-30}}</ref>

His later work, building on the application of silicon in organic chemistry he had developed, included the synthesis of the [[natural products]] [[thienamycin]],<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Fleming |first1=Ian |last2=Kilburn |first2=Jeremy D. |title=Stereocontrol in organic synthesis using silicon-containing compounds. A formal synthesis of (±)-thienamycin |journal=Journal of the Chemical Society, Perkin Transactions 1 |date=1998 |issue=17 |pages=2663–2672 |doi=10.1039/A804271C }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Breunig |first1=Jamie L. |last2=Lin |first2=You-Chen |last3=Pierce |first3=Joshua G. |title=An enantioselective formal synthesis of thienamycin |journal=Tetrahedron Letters |date=2024 |volume=144 |article-number=155132 |doi=10.1016/j.tetlet.2024.155132 |pmid=39006392 |pmc=11242926 }}</ref> [[nonactin]],<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Fleming |first1=Ian |last2=Ghosh |first2=Sunil K. |title=Stereocontrol in organic synthesis using silicon-containing compounds. A synthesis of nonactin |journal=Journal of the Chemical Society, Perkin Transactions 1 |date=1998 |issue=17 |pages=2733–2748 |doi=10.1039/A804284E }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Gustafson |first1=Afton |last2=Kahr |first2=Bart |title=Optical Activity of Nonactin and Its Cation Complexes |journal=Chirality |date=2024 |volume=36 |issue=8 |article-number=e23703 |doi=10.1002/chir.23703 |pmid=39034362 }}</ref> and [[sparteine]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Buttler |first1=Thomas |last2=Fleming |first2=Ian |last3=Gonsior |first3=Sabine |last4=Kim |first4=Bo-Hye |last5=Sung |first5=A.-Young |last6=Woo |first6=Hee-Gweon |title=A synthesis of (±)-sparteine |journal=Org. Biomol. Chem. |date=2005 |volume=3 |issue=8 |pages=1557–1567 |doi=10.1039/B502213D |doi-access=free |pmid=15827657 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Firth |first1=James D. |last2=Canipa |first2=Steven J. |last3=Ferris |first3=Leigh |last4=O'Brien |first4=Peter |title=Gram-Scale Synthesis of the (−)-Sparteine Surrogate and (−)-Sparteine |journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition |date=2018 |volume=57 |issue=1 |pages=223–226 |doi=10.1002/anie.201710261 |url=https://pure.york.ac.uk/portal/files/53543155/Surrogate_Sparteine_manuscript_AAM.pdf |pmid=29155468 }}</ref>

==Personal life==
Fleming married Mary Bernard, an author, in 1965;<ref>{{cite news |work=[[Telegraph-Journal]] |issn=0837-3736 |title=George Frederick Clarke makes a comeback |location=New Brunswick |last=Muise |first=Jackie |date=12 September 2015 |page=F4 |via=newspapers.com}}</ref> they have no children.<ref name=cv/> His interests include photography and he has taken portraits of every Pembroke College Fellow since 1963.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.pem.cam.ac.uk/college/news/portraits-women-fellows-hall |title=Portraits of Women Fellows in the Hall |date=May 2014 |website=pem.cam.ac.uk |access-date=2025-10-02 }}</ref> Some of his work is included in the 2025 book which describes the buildings and gardens of the college.<ref>{{cite book |url=https://www.google.co.uk/books/edition/Pembroke_College_Cambridge/sb7R0AEACAAJ?hl=en |title=Pembroke College, Cambridge: The Buildings and Gardens |editor-last=Smith |editor-first=Chris |editor-link=Chris Smith, Baron Smith of Finsbury |isbn=9781785515330 |year=2025 |page=159}}</ref> Fleming has been credited as being one of those who actively campaigned for the admission of women to Pembroke.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.pem.cam.ac.uk/college/news/march-2025-nami-morris-deputy-development-director |title=March 2025 - Nami Morris, Deputy Development Director |date=March 2025 |last=Morris |first=Nami |website=pem.cam.ac.uk |access-date=2025-10-02 }}</ref>
